hypothesis: Within the preregistered noisy latent-order family, an exact F_T-minimizing order learned from one tournament predicts an independent tournament better than an independent random order, and its mean held-out error is nondecreasing with the injected noise level.
alternatives: The learned F_T-minimizing orders have no positive aggregate predictive advantage over independent random orders.
Mean held-out error is not nondecreasing across the preregistered noise levels.
The result depends on vertex labels or the generator fails to inject exactly the declared number of reversals.

observables.measure: training/test masks, latent order, fitted minimum and held-out scores for every pair
exact trained, control and oracle violation totals at every noise level
random-control violations minus trained-order violations over all held-out tournaments
number of adjacent noise levels where mean trained held-out error decreases
number of samples changed by the preregistered transported relabelling
number of test tournaments whose latent-order score differs from the injected flip count

controls.purpose: Test whether the learned order beats a seed-generated order independent of both tournaments.
Verify that transported vertex relabelling preserves both the training minimum and held-out score.
Verify that each test tournament contains exactly the declared number of reversals relative to its latent order.

analysis.stoppingRule: Execute exactly 48 independent training/test pairs at each of the four declared flip counts in one primary run. After sealing, permit one deterministic reconstruction solely for byte comparison; never add samples or change thresholds.
analysis.comparisonPlan: Require strictly positive aggregate predictive advantage, zero adjacent monotonicity violations, zero representation mismatches and zero oracle mismatches. Apply only the four locked reversal conditions.
